Levelek Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Levelek, Hungary

Not demolished. Levelek's Jewish cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map and was gradually enlarged over time, with its fenced section's newest tombstone dated 1944. Population peaked at 203 in 1910, falling to 100 by 1941. The Orthodox community maintained a burial society and mikveh; a wealthy member funded both the synagogue and an elementary school (later closed, leaving only a cheder). Several villagers died in WWI service; the fall of 1918 and subsequent 1920 Romanian occupation brought repeated antisemitic violence - officers stormed the synagogue during the 'White Terror' period, beating worshippers, and Jews were also attacked at school, prompting several families to flee. By 1944, only 91 Jews remained in the village; a 1949 postwar census found just 11, and soon after only a single Jewish resident remained.
